speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they appeared suddenly or gradually?

Have you noticed any fever, fatigue, or joint pain accompanying these skin and mouth lesions?

To better understand the severity, could you describe the appearance of the blisters and ulcers, and have you experienced any eye pain or vision changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Multiforme Major. The patient's recent initiation of captopril, combined with mucosal involvement (oral and genital) and cutaneous lesions, strongly suggests a drug-induced hypersensitivity reaction. Please confirm if the blisters on the forearm are targetoid (iris-like) in appearance and if you have noticed any fever or flu-like symptoms in the past week.
